correctness.rationale: For \(0<\theta<1\) the symbol is a disk self-map with one boundary contact. Its H2 power norms have exact Laplace constant A_theta and H1 norms decay like \(n^{-1/\theta}\). Paley gives a uniform \(O(n^{-2/\theta})\) correction for changed output coefficients, so normalized input spike columns have squared norms asymptotic to A_theta \(b^{j(\alpha-1/\theta)}(j\log b)^\gamma\). Summing proves all HS and unbounded regimes and both Abelian residues. At \(\alpha=1/\theta\) \(\gamma=0\), normalized cusp powers have a geometrically Schur-bounded Gram matrix; multiplying input spike columns by log^{gamma/2}->0 proves critical compactness when \(\gamma<0\). At \(\gamma=0\) unit spike vectors are weakly null with nonvanishing output norms, hence noncompact. The finite companion script passes 817 checks, corroborative only; none of the proof uses finite truncation as infinite evidence.

value.rationale: The recently studied class-equality questions leave concrete symbol behavior open when lacunary coefficient weights create deep troughs. This result gives a sharp natural boundary of a regular parameter family: a nontrivial compact/non-Hilbert–Schmidt phase between an exact \(\gamma=-1\) ideal threshold and \(\gamma=0\) essential-norm obstruction. Exact two independent HS blow-up residues quantitatively explain the transition and support further singular-value work.
